title: 2.5D
summary: 2.5D describes gameplay or movement restricted to a 2D plane within a simulated 3D environment, creating the appearance of three dimensions through projection techniques rather than true 3D rendering. It differs from pseudo-3D by focusing on restricted plane movement, and from true 2D by approximating a 3D image. The term originates from portraying faces partway between frontal and side views, and common applications include axonometric projection, billboarding, Z-axis scaling, and parallax scrolling to convey depth cues.

mechanisms.title: Axonometric and oblique projection
mechanisms.explanation: Rotates the viewpoint slightly in parallel projection to reveal facets beyond a top-down or side view, producing a three-dimensional effect through foreshortening of inclined axes. Combines top-down visibility with side-scrolling character recognizability, allowing the player to see the entire body and side views while maintaining an overview.

mechanisms.title: Billboarding and Z-axis scaling
mechanisms.explanation: Represents 3D objects with 2D images kept perpendicular to the line of sight (billboarding), commonly used for distant geometry like particles and vegetation to boost performance. Scales sprites larger or smaller based on distance along the Z axis, such as in Out Run, where background elements are scaled to create forward motion illusion despite restricted movement.
